exposure: Body mass index (BMI) before first pregnancy
cohort: 121,092 women from the Missouri maternally linked birth registry (1989-2005)
finding: Women with suboptimal BMI (underweight or obese) in their first pregnancy had increased risks of adverse maternal and fetal outcomes in their second pregnancy, even if the first pregnancy was uncomplicated.
mod_finding: Compared to women with a normal BMI in their first pregnancy, those with prepregnancy obesity had increased odds for cesarean delivery in their second pregnancy by 85%.
